items.titel: Linking Carbon Footprints to Air-Pollutant Emissions from Mega Sporting Events: Evidence from the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics
items.samenvatting_bron: Mega sporting events report carbon footprints, but rarely describe the air pollutants that accompany them. This study links the verified greenhouse-gas inventory of the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics (713,788 t CO2e, 2016–2022) to co-emitted NOx, SO2, PM2.5, CO and NMVOC in a screening-level, emission-side assessment using eight emission carriers with Chinese pollutant-to-CO2 ratios, Shapley attribution, and Monte Carlo and Sobol analyses. Construction accounted for 63% of the CO2e, an estimated 70% of the 1335 t of NOx, and 76% of the 279 t of PM2.5, remaining the largest NOx source in 99.9–100% of uncertainty draws and under alternative attributions. The measures taken, chiefly the employment of green electricity, avoided 31% of no-measure emissions and 18% of NOx under market-based accounting, but only 8% of NOx if green certificates were not used. Under literature-based assumptions, eight additional levers could have cut CO2e by 46% (41–53%) and NOx by 49%; zero-emission construction machinery avoids the most NOx per tonne of CO2. A residual of 384,375 t would remain; the offsets retired (2.4 times the emissions) reduced no air pollutants. For construction-dominated events, such as this pandemic-era edition, climate- and air-quality co-benefits are decided largely at the design stage, through materials and machinery, rather than by offsetting.

items.titel: Governance pathways shape trophic recovery under climate change in the western Mediterranean Sea
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Marine ecosystems are increasingly shaped by the interacting effects of climate change and human activities, yet the extent to which alternative socio-economic pathways can modify future ecological trajectories remains poorly understood. Here, we integrate climate projections with coherent socioecological scenarios to evaluate long-term ecosystem responses in the western Mediterranean Sea. Using a spatially explicit marine ecosystem model (Ecopath with Ecosim) representing 92 functional groups and five fishing fleets, we simulated ecosystem dynamics from 1995 to 2020 and projected changes to 2100 under contrasting pathways combining climate forcing, fisheries management, marine protection, and habitat restoration. Scenarios included a sustainability-oriented pathway (SSP1–RCP2.6; Global Sustainability), two high-emission pathways with contrasting governance (SSP3–RCP8.5; National Enterprise and SSP5–RCP8.5; World Markets), and associated status quo baselines. Socio-economic pathways substantially modified the ecological outcomes of climate change. Under Global Sustainability, reduced fishing pressure, expanded marine protection, discard mitigation, and habitat restoration promoted rapid rebuilding of commercial and predatory biomass, recovery of conservation-relevant species, and improved trophic structure within two decades, although fisheries catches declined. items.titel: Challenges of Over-Urbanization and Pressure on Critical Infrastructure
items.samenvatting_bron: In today’s world of rapid global change, the topic of challenges of over-urbanization and pressure on critical infrastructure is becoming more and more significant. To mention a few, they are: Urbanization trends, strain on resources, environmental impact, socioeconomic inequality, and need for sustainable solutions. Urbanization trends show us that more than half of the global population now resides in urban areas, and projections suggest that this figure will rise to two-thirds by 2050. Cities are becoming the focal points of human activity and economic growth. This rapid urbanization brings about significant challenges, particularly in managing the infrastructure that supports urban life ( National Geographic, 2024 ). In terms of the impact on resources, over-urbanization causes overcrowding, which puts tremendous strain on the vital infrastructure that is now in place, such as energy supplies, water supply, transportation systems, and sanitary facilities. The demand for these services frequently exceeds supply as cities grow, leaving citizens with subpar amenities and services. Deteriorating living circumstances, worsening traffic, and worsening environmental degradation can all result from this strain. The effects of excessive urbanization on the environment are significant. Loss of green space, increased garbage output, and pollution of the air and water are common outcomes of urban expansion. items.titel: Green economic transformation and environmental security: Policy pathways toward sustainable resilience
items.samenvatting_bron: The global community confronts escalating environmental crises, including anthropogenic climate change, biodiversity loss, and resource depletion, which collectively threaten planetary boundaries and human well-being. The "green economy" paradigm and the concept of "environmental security" are pivotal for addressing these challenges and fostering sustainable development. The aim of this study is to synthesize current academic discourse on green economic transformation and its implications for environmental security and sustainable resilience. This systematic literature review analyzed peer-reviewed publications from 2020 to the present, sourced from Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, focusing on interconnections between green economic principles, environmental security challenges, and policy mechanisms. The review reveals multifaceted policy pathways, highlighting fiscal recovery packages as crucial for accelerating investments in green infrastructure and sustainable transitions, and regulatory frameworks as pivotal for a circular economy. It further indicates that green economic policies directly enhance environmental security by mitigating climate change, biodiversity loss, and resource depletion, with investments in green infrastructure building resilience against climate impacts. items.titel: The densified city and the powerline right-of-way encroachment in Nigeria: Greening as an important intervention.
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban densification is generally promoted as a strategy for sustainable development. However, it may also produce unintended consequences, such as exposure to environmental hazards. This study examines potential electrical hazard exposure in relation to the powerline right-of-way (ROW) encroachment in Port Harcourt Metropolis, a rapidly densifying oil and gas industry hub in southern Nigeria, using a mixed-method approach that combines geospatial datasets and social survey data. The Pressure and Release (PAR) framework is used primarily as an interpretive framework for organizing observed spatial conditions and respondents' reported reasons for and experiences in occupying buildings within the powerline ROW. The findings show that about 256 buildings are located within the powerline ROW. Among surveyed occupants, 58.3% reported access to infrastructure and 20.0% reported proximity to livelihood sources as reasons for occupying buildings within the ROW. No electrical accidents were reported, while 50% of respondents reported powerline sagging and 12.2% reported arc flash. The study suggests green infrastructure as a policy option for managing the powerline ROW by transforming it into a managed ecological corridor that could help reduce encroachment and provide environmental benefits. items.titel: Homemaking amid uncertainty: Russian newcomers and host communities in post-2022 Tbilisi
items.samenvatting_bron: This article examines homemaking practices among both Russian newcomers and host communities in Tbilisi, Georgia, exploring how change, uncertainty, and migrant-host relations shape the making and unmaking of home. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork conducted in 2023–24 with socially aware, economically non-privileged Russian migrants who oppose the war in Ukraine, and ongoing participant observation in Tbilisi, the article traces two interconnected processes: how host community responses to Russian migration constitute their own forms of homemaking and claiming of belonging, and how some Russian migrants enact quiet, often non-material homemaking practices – walking familiar routes, building online communities, participating in Tbilisi protests – amid constrained and contested circumstances. Situating homemaking at the intersection of migration studies and critical geographies of home, the article argues that home is not a possession but a relational and contested practice, unfolding across mobilities, memory, politics, and everyday life. Central to this argument is the role of non-human actors – streets, urban green spaces, animals, and digital platforms – as active participants in homemaking. items.samenvatting_bron: Aquatic toxicology is rapidly evolving from conventional single-contaminant toxicity testing toward an integrated discipline capable of addressing complex chemical mixtures, emerging contaminants, climate-related stressors, and ecosystem-level responses. Aquatic ecosystems are increasingly exposed to pharmaceuticals, pesticides, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), microplastics, nanoplastics, nanoparticles, industrial chemicals, antibiotics and transformation products. At the same time, climate change, eutrophication, habitat alteration and changing hydrological conditions can modify contaminant fate, bioavailability and toxicity. Recent advances in high-resolution mass spectrometry, non-target chemical analysis, multi-omics, environmental DNA (eDNA), adverse outcome pathways (AOPs), exposomics, biosensors and artificial intelligence are transforming aquatic toxicology. Emerging research increasingly emphasizes environmentally realistic concentrations, chronic exposure, mixture toxicity, trophic transfer and interactions between chemical and non-chemical stressors. items.titel: Large-volume sampling enhances eDNA monitoring of endangered marine species
items.samenvatting_bron: Environmental DNA (eDNA) has emerged as a powerful tool for detecting marine biodiversity, particularly for monitoring elusive or endangered species. However, traditional eDNA sampling protocols often rely on small water volumes (≤2 L), which can limit detection sensitivity, especially in vast and dynamic marine environments. Here, we evaluated the effectiveness of large-volume eDNA enrichment (5–50 L) for improving the detection probability of endangered marine species, using metabarcoding and quantitative PCR (qPCR) designed for Balaenoptera brydei (Bryde’s Whale). Results showed that the capsule sampler, equipped with a highly folded filter membrane, can filter over 50 L of seawater, significantly increasing eDNA yield and species detection rates compared to standard small-volume sampling (1 L). For metabarcoding results, the large-volume sampling also yielded more total eDNA sequence reads from marine vertebrates and from the endangered Beibu Gulf population of Bryde’s Whale, enabling more robust detection of endangered species. Furthermore, combining metabarcoding and qPCR provided complementary detection capabilities for monitoring endangered marine mammals, with metabarcoding enabling broad-spectrum screening and qPCR providing target-specific quantification. items.titel: Drivers of mosquito presence and abundance in urban and garden ponds in a European city
items.samenvatting_bron: Abstract Mosquitoes in urban environments are considered unpleasant by citizens, and they can represent serious health risks as vectors of pathogens. Invasive Aedes species are continuously spreading in Europe and have been increasingly reported from urban settlements. Some of these mosquito species have been associated with small artificial habitats. Therefore, their presence may also be expected in small plastic garden ponds, which are numerous in urban settings across many parts of Europe. Here, we aimed to determine whether urban waters host a high abundance of mosquitoes and to identify the potential abiotic, biotic and landscape drivers of mosquito presence and abundance in urban ponds. We sampled 93 urban ponds in the city of Budapest (Hungary), comprising 40 garden ponds and 53 other urban ponds of both natural and anthropogenic origin, across highly urbanised areas and suburban areas with a high green index. We collected data on macroinvertebrate communities, pond management, physico-chemical parameters, and pond characteristics (mainly morphology and vegetation cover) measured in situ . items.titel: AI-Driven Unified Data Platform for Oceano-graphic, Fisheries, and Molecular Biodiversity Insights: A Review
items.samenvatting_bron: Marine ecosystems produce heterogeneous data from satellites, buoys, research vessels, fisheries activity, laboratory sequencing, and environmental DNA (eDNA) sampling. These sources can reveal ocean conditions, fish distribution, ecosystem change, and biodiversity, but are often stored in separate systems with incompatible formats and metadata. Artificial intelligence (AI) can support forecasting, anomaly detection, habitat modelling, fisheries analysis, and molecular classification. This review examines deep learning for marine water-quality assessment, wireless sensor networks, hybrid models for aquaculture, and molecular biodiversity workflows. It proposes a conceptual unified platform with secure ingestion, source-aware storage, metadata harmonisation, data fusion, AI analytics, and decision-support dashboards. Major challenges include uneven sampling, data interoperability, sensor drift, uncertain labels, model transferability, computational cost, and governance of sensitive fisheries and biodiversity data. The platform is a review-derived architecture rather than an implemented or experimentally validated system.

items.titel: Estimating the urban heat island effect with lichens and bryophytes: a citizen science protocol
items.samenvatting_bron: The urban heat island effect (UHI), whereby urban areas are warmer than the surrounding rural areas, has become an increasing threat to human health and affects biodiversity. Counteracting this public health concern requires large-scale monitoring of urban heat. One cost-effective way to obtain this data is by using bioindicators, such as lichens and bryophytes. They are well-known bioindicators readily available in the urban environment, and have proven to respond to the UHI. Gathering large amounts of data in a short time span may prove difficult for many institutes or municipalities, but can be resolved by incorporating citizen science. However, lichen and bryophyte species identification with no prior experience may prove problematic for citizen scientists. Therefore, we developed a citizen science protocol that requires scoring the presence of easily recognisable morphotypes of epiphytic lichens and bryophytes, instead of individual species. Data was collected in urban environments in the Netherlands by participants at three knowledge levels: an expert in lichenology and bryology, university biology students, and citizen scientists. Using the expert dataset, we trained a baseline multiple linear model (LM) and a random forest (RF) model, which predicted local UHI with low root-mean-square errors (RMSE = 0.29 °C and 0.20 °C, respectively). items.titel: Nature-Based Solutions for Urban Microclimate Resilience in Hot Arid Regions
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban areas in hot-arid regions face extreme temperatures, water scarcity, and deteriorating air quality, intensified by rapid urbanization and climate change. This study evaluates nature-based solution (NBS) configurations in a road-widened street corridor in Zahraa El Maadi, Cairo, Egypt. Seven ENVI-met 5.9.0 scenarios, varying in tree-canopy, grass, green-roof, and water coverage, were compared over a 24 h peak-summer period. Air temperature (Ta), wind speed (WS), relative humidity (RH), and physiological equivalent temperature (PET) were assessed at three pedestrian-level receptors at 12:00, 16:00, and 20:00, and i-Tree MyTree was used to estimate complementary carbon, runoff, and air-quality co-benefits for a representative Ficus microcarpa tree. items.titel: Desafios e perspectivas para o fortalecimento da infraestrutura hospitalar diante das mudanças climáticas
items.samenvatting_bron: Climate change has intensified the occurrence of extreme hydrological events, such as floods, inundations, and landslides, generating significant impacts on urban infrastructure and healthcare systems. In this context, this study analyzes the challenges and prospects for adapting hospitals located in areas exposed to water-related disasters, considering the effects of climate change on healthcare capacity and hospital infrastructure. The research is characterized as exploratory and descriptive, using a qualitative approach based on a bibliographic and documentary review of scientific articles, institutional reports, and official documents related to climate change, public health, and risk management. The findings indicate that hydrological disasters compromise hospital physical structures, cause operational disruptions, reduce bed availability, and increase demand for emergency healthcare services. Emergency departments, diagnostic imaging units, and surgical centers were identified as the most vulnerable sectors during extreme events. The analysis also demonstrated that the lack of preventive planning, deficiencies in drainage systems, and the location of hospitals in flood-prone areas increase institutional risks. items.titel: The missing measurement behind urban nature-based solutions resilience claims
items.samenvatting_bron: Nature-based solutions (NbS) have become a central component of urban climate adaptation strategies, yet the indicators used to support resilience claims do not always reflect resilience as a system property. Many studies interpret short-term environmental improvements as evidence of resilience, although such indicators rarely capture the capacity of urban systems to withstand disturbances, adapt to changing conditions, and recover over time. This review applies an Output–Outcome–Impact–Resilience (OOIR) framework to a set of 97 urban NbS sources, identified through a structured, PRISMA-guided search of the Scopus and Web of Science databases, published between 2015 and 2025 to examine how resilience is operationalised in practice. Impact-level indicators were the most common, accounting for 53.6% of the sources, followed by outcome-level (26.8%) and output-level indicators (19.6%). Of the 97 sources reviewed, 62 (63.9%) explicitly claimed a contribution to resilience, yet 34 of these 62 (54.8%) supported that claim solely with impact-level indicators. Under the OOIR framework used in this study, none of the reviewed sources included indicators that met the criteria for direct resilience measurement. Governance-related sources accounted for the largest share of the set, whereas economic indicators remained rare. items.samenvatting_bron: Het kabinet praat vandaag in het Catshuis verder met de oppositie over het belastingplan. Er is vanochtend een intern overleg geweest tussen premier Jetten, de vicepremiers Yesilgöz en Van den Brink en minister Heinen en staatssecretaris Eerenberg van Financiën. Daarna komen de partijleiders Bikker (ChristenUnie) en Struijs (50Plus) langs. Samen met de Groep Markuszower, waar officieel nog niet mee is onderhandeld, kunnen zij het minderheidskabinet in de Tweede Kamer aan een meerderheid helpen. Digitaal gesprek Daarna is er een digitaal gesprek met de partijleiders Eerdmans (JA21), Vermeer (BBB) en Stoffer (SGP). Dit 'bondje' van rechtse partijen komt op eigen verzoek niet in Den Haag langs. De drie vingen gisteren bot wat betreft hun aanbod het belastingplan te steunen, mits er aan een aantal voorwaarden wordt voldaan. Die hebben onder meer betrekking op asiel, stikstof en abortus en draagmoederschap. De coalitiepartijen D66 en CDA hebben daar grote moeite mee. Vanmiddag komen Pro en Volt naar het Catshuis.
